## 1e07c169ac61

**Issue found: the generator collapses “rotate around the color-9 anchor” into “rotate around the grid center,” and its grammar rejects canonical inputs.**

Every generated anchor is fixed at `(h // 2, w // 2)`, every blob is a single monochrome 4-connected object strictly above-left of it, and `self_check` enforces those restrictions. However, canonical train input 1 has the anchor at `(3,2)` in a `6x6` grid, not at `(3,3)`, and canonical train input 0 also has a foreground cell outside the strict upper-left quadrant. Directly calling the shipped `self_check` rejects both canonical training inputs.

The second canonical training input is already an exact counterexample:

```text
input
000000
000400
000400
009440
000000
000000
```

Rotating around the actual color-9 anchor at `(3,2)` gives the canonical output:

```text
000000
000000
000000
009000
004440
004000
```

A solver trained only on this generator can instead leave the 9 in place but rotate all other cells around the geometric center `(3,3)`; on every generated grid the two pivots coincide. On this canonical input that shortcut gives:

```text
000000
000000
000000
009444
000400
000000
```

The generator should vary the anchor over legal in-bounds positions, place foreground in multiple quadrants, and include multicolor/disconnected cases because the canonical rule acts on every nonzero, non-9 cell independently while preserving color. `self_check` should accept all canonical inputs and validate the actual pivot semantics rather than a centered-upper-left presentation prior.
